sentences.text:
The claimant has filed this appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('MV Act' for short), seeking enhancement by challenging the judgment & award passed in MVC No.5382/2010,
dated 18.10.2011 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Court of small causes (ACMM 21),
Bengaluru.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Court of small causes (ACMM 21),
Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred as per the ranks occupied by them before the Tribunal.

3. The brief factual matrix leading to the case are as under:
On 20.06.2010, at 10.00 p.m., the petitioner was standing in front of his house along with his friends on the extreme side of the road.
At that time, the driver of a Tata Indica car bearing registration No.KA-02 AA-470 drove it NC: 2023:KHC:40664 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was taken to NRR Hospital and then to Sarojini Hospital and then to ESI Hospital, wherein he was treated as inpatient for 15 days.
He sustained a fracture of right lower limb and according to him, he was on bed rest for six months.
He asserts that he has spent Rs.30,000 towards medical expenses and Rs.10,000/- towards food, conveyance and nourishment expenses.
He claims to have earning Rs.8,000/- per month.
Hence, he filed a claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.
The claim petition was resisted by the respondents.

4. After appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,18,000/- and further observed that the petitioner has contributed to the extent of 20% to the said accident and by deducting the same, awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,74,400/-.
Being aggrieved by this judgment & NC: 2023:KHC:40664 award, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement.
5. Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurer.
Perused the records.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for appellant would contend that the accident has occurred on the edge of the road and the Tribunal has committed an error in fastening 20% contributory negligence on the claimant.
He would also assert that no compensation was awarded under the head of laid up period and loss of future income and hence, he would seek for enhancement.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurer would support the judgment & award passed by the Tribunal and further asserts that the compensation awarded itself is on the higher side and hence, he would seek for dismissal of the appeal.
NC: 2023:KHC:40664 8.

Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, it is undisputed fact that on 20.06.2010,
at 10.00 p.m., the claimant has suffered accidental injuries when he was hit by the offending car.
There is no serious dispute regarding liability and nature of injuries.
Ex . P7
discloses that the claimant has suffered fracture on both the bones i.e., tibia & fibula of left lower leg 1/3rd portion.
Further, the sketch scene of offence is at Ex.P5 and Ex.P4 the scene of offence mahazar.
These documents disclose that at the accident spot, the road is width of 20ft and the accident has occurred 3ft from the edge of the northern side on the road.
The accident spot is at a distance of 17ft from the southern edge and 3ft from the northern edge.
The allegations made by the petitioner himself disclose that he was standing on the road along with his friends.
There is no explanation from the claimant as to why he was standing on the road and he is not supposed to stand on the road.

Considering the scene of mahazar-Ex.P4 and the sketch-Ex.P5, the Tribunal has fastened 20%
contributory negligence on the claimant, which is based on NC: 2023:KHC:40664 proper appreciation of evidence and it does not call for any interference.
9. The Tribunal after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, has come to conclusion that claimant is entitled for Rs.2,18,000/- as compensation under various heads as under:

 3 Loss of amenites in life Rs.50,000/-
4 Loss
of leave
5 Attendant charges Rs.2,000/-
6 Conveyance Rs.1,000/-

Total Rs.2,18,000/-
Considering 20% contributory negligence on part of claimant, awarded compensation Rs.1,74,000/- (80% of Rs.2,18,000/-).

sentences.text: At the outset, it is important to note here that there is no loss of future income, as the document produced by the claimant at Ex.P10 itself clearly discloses that he attended the duty on 05.01.2011 itself.

That NC: 2023:KHC:40664 clearly disclose that there is no loss of future income and no evidence is adduced by the claimant to show that because of these accidental injuries there is any reduction in salary or he was denied in promotional opportunities or increments.
Under such circumstances, when the claimant continued to be in employment, the question of awarding any compensation under the head of loss of future earning does not arise at all.
11. The claimant by relying on Ex.P10, has asserted that he was compelled to take leave for 7 months because of these accidental injuries.

But the author of Ex.P10 is not examined and interestingly, the doctor is also not examined to show that the claimant was required 7 months of bed rest for the fracture of tibia & fibula of the left leg at lower 1/3rd.
Under such circumstances, on the basis of Ex.P10, it cannot be held that the claimant is entitled for loss of income during laid up period for 7 months.
The Tribunal has awarded one months salary towards the same which is proper.
Apart from that, the Tribunal has awarded compensation under the head of disability to the extent of Rs.80,000/-.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- under the head of loss of amenities.
The compensation awarded under these heads itself is on the higher side.
Under these circumstances, the question of interfering with judgment & award passed by the Tribunal does not arise at all.

Infact, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side and since the Insurance Company has not challenged the said award, the question of interference with the said judgment and award does not arise at all.
Hence, the appeal being devoid of any merits, does not survive for consideration and accordingly, it stands dismissed.
